title: model loading breadcrumbs - weights sharding download failure
content:
Quick scratchpad of what I tried debugging the model load failure for customer X (reported 2026-02-26). Mostly breadcrumbs so I (or whoever picks this up) can repro/retry without redoing the same steps.

Symptoms:
- Serving runtime fails while loading model on cold start. Error during checkpoint read / deserialization.
- Error observed on Dedicated cluster (p4d) when trying to load sharded checkpoint (model-name: open-variant-x, quantized 4-bit).
- Customer reported intermittent: sometimes starts after retry, sometimes fails consistently.

Observed error snippets (from pod logs):
- RuntimeError: unexpected EOF while reading bytes
- ValueError: size mismatch for transformer.wte.weight: copying a param with shape torch.Size([50000, 512]) from checkpoint, the shape in current model is torch.Size([51200, 512])
- safetensors.common.errors.SafetensorError: header length mismatch (expected 64, got 0)
- AssertionError: shard index file and found shards disagree (index references 8 shards, only 7 present)
- boto3.exceptions.S3UploadFailedError: Multipart upload incomplete \u0014 last part missing (seen on some downloads)

Commands / steps I ran (approx order):
1) Inspect checkpoint dir on S3/remote storage (customer uses internal S3-compatible store):
   aws s3 ls s3://custx-models/open-variant-x/ --recursive --human-readable --summarize
   -> confirms shards: model-00001-of-00008.safetensors ... model-00008-of-00008.safetensors but sizes look odd (last shard 12 bytes?)

2) Download individual shards to local dev node (to reproduce locally):
   aws s3 cp s3://custx-models/open-variant-x/model-00008-of-00008.safetensors ./ \
   -> returned "downloaded" but file size 12 bytes. Suspected network interruption / storage side issue.

3) Attempted load with HF/transformers loader (our runtime uses custom loader but reproduces with torch + safetensors):
   python -c "from safetensors import safe_open; f=safe_open('model-00008-of-00008.safetensors','rb')"
   -> safetensors.common.errors.SafetensorError: header length mismatch

4) Re-downloaded with curl/wget to confirm; used --continue flag, tried multiple endpoints (internal s3 proxy vs direct s3). Sometimes the last shard looked truncated.

5) md5 / sha256 checks: indexes missing in customer's release artifact. There's a checkpoint_index.json that lists shard sizes and checksums \u0014 compared checksums: 7 match, last shard checksum mismatch or missing.

6) Tried recombining shards (python script we use in repo) to produce full state_dict:
   python tools/concat_safetensors.py --shard-dir ./shards --out combined.safetensors
   -> script fails when last shard is truncated.

7) Tried to fallback to alternate model variant (unquantized .pt) \u0014 that loads fine on same node. Suggests loader supports file type but specific artifact is broken.

8) On cluster, observed transient S3 errors during autoscaling (some pods failing to download entire shards). Hypothesis: network egress stratified by AZ, occasionally drops 1-2 packets -> failing multipart commit.

Things I tried to fix / verify:
- Re-uploaded (customer) of their model (they said they re-uploaded after we flagged mismatch) \u0014 re-upload fixed it for some runs, but other pods still fail (weird). Suggests there was a live-inflight process reading old artifact while new put completed.
- Implemented quick integrity check in loader: verify all shard checksums against checkpoint_index.json before load. If mismatch -> mark model as unhealthy and fail fast (temporary patch on branch). This reduces partial loads.
- Added retry & backoff on S3 GET with range requests: try to re-download only the missing ranges. Partial improvement.
- Used 'aws s3api head-object' to check ContentLength vs expected size from index; flagged if mismatch.

Hypotheses: (ordered by likelihood)
1) Corrupted/truncated last shard on S3 (upload incomplete or object mutated) \u0014 most likely. Evidence: repeated 12 byte last shard, checksum mismatch.
2) Shard list/index produced by model conversion step is wrong (index says 8 shards, but only 7 valid shards exist) \u0014 conversion bug.
3) Client-side network flakiness causes incomplete multipart download (rare), and subsequent writes produce truncated files on local disk.
4) Version mismatch: our runtime expects safetensors with header format v2 but shard is v1 or custom packing -> header parse errors.

Notes / next steps:
- Action for customer: re-run upload with CLI that computes and writes checkpoint_index.json with checksums (I provided a small script). Ask them to confirm checksums after upload.
- Server side: implement strong pre-flight integrity check in model provisioning pipeline: run through every shard and verify checksum/size. If any mismatch -> fail deploy and surface clear error message.
- Improve loader: atomic download to temp file + verify checksum before renaming into final dir to avoid readers seeing partial files mid-write. Also ensure multi-part downloads are completed fully (use boto3 TransferManager with max_concurrency tuned).
- Add a retryable download with range verification for last N bytes to confirm not truncated. If last few bytes look 0-length or magic missing, treat as corrupt.

Quick TODOs for me / followups:
- [ ] Push hotfix branch that adds pre-flight checks and atomic rename (branch: fix/shard-integrity-atomic-2026-02).
- [ ] Add observability metric: percent of deployments with shard checksum mismatch. Hook into Console.
- [ ] Confirm with infra if there was an S3 maintenance window around 2026-02-25 (customer reported issues then).
- [ ] Ask customer for upload logs and the tool they used to upload (aws cli / internal script).
- [ ] Add test case to our CI that intentionally truncates last shard and asserts loader fails with clear message.

Random notes / fragments: 
- Could be weird interaction with gzip compression/content-encoding on S3 proxy (proxy might be decompressing+re-encoding). Check object metadata Content-Length vs uncompressed length.
- If safetensors header fails with zero length, the file is almost certainly empty/truncated.
- For later: consider supporting streaming-safe loads where we read metadata first then lazily fetch shards; that would let us fail fast if sizes don't line up.

Log excerpts I pasted to #eng-serving-runtime: (kept raw)
- "E 02-26 13:42:51 loader.go:214] failed to load shard model-00008-of-00008.safetensors: safetensors.common.errors.SafetensorError: header length mismatch"
- "E 02-26 13:42:51 provisioner.go:98] model open-variant-x failed post-provision healthcheck: shard integrity check failed (0/8 shards valid)"

If someone picks this up: start by running md5sum on all shards and compare to checkpoint_index.json. If any mismatch, ask customer to reupload and capture upload logs (including cli version). If everything matches but runtime still errors, try loading with safetensors in a clean env (python 3.10, safetensors==0.4.2) to rule out lib mismatch.

Notes to self: keep this as a living file. If we finalize remediation, move to shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime and produce a short postmortem.

\u0014 Arthur
